text: History of falling: A documented occurrence of one or more falls, indicating potential underlying balance, gait, or neurological issues. Common presenting complaints: Falls. Associated symptoms: Dizziness, Gait Instability, Fear Of Falling, Orthostatic Hypotension. Risk factors: Previousfalls, Age, Polypharmacy, Visualimpairment. Age relevance: . Sex relevance: . History of falling red flags. Red flag (RF_SEVERE_HEAD_INJURY_POST_FALL) triggered by complaint 'FALLS': [LLM DRAFT] Patient has experienced a fall resulting in loss of consciousness, severe headache, confusion, or neurological deficits.. Red flag (RF_SUSPECTED_MAJOR_FRACTURE_POST_FALL) triggered by complaint 'FALLS': [LLM DRAFT] Patient has experienced a fall resulting in severe localized pain, inability to bear weight, or obvious skeletal deformity..

History of falling differential diagnosis notes. Compared to Parkinsons Disease Without Dyskinesia With Fluctuations: [LLM DRAFT] Presence of resting tremor, rigidity, and bradykinesia accompanied by motor fluctuations. Compared to Other Idiopathic Peripheral Autonomic Neuropathy: [LLM DRAFT] Prominent orthostatic hypotension, anhidrosis, or gastrointestinal dysmotility without central motor signs.

Other idiopathic peripheral autonomic neuropathy: A rare, unexplained peripheral autonomic neuropathy presenting with orthostatic intolerance, sweating abnormalities, and gastrointestinal dysmotility. Common presenting complaints: Falls. Associated symptoms: Shooting Pain, Numbness, Tingling, Tremors, Bladder Problems, Unsteadiness. Risk factors: none listed. Age relevance: . Sex relevance: . Acute or chronic: .

Other idiopathic peripheral autonomic neuropathy red flags. Red flag (RF_AUTONOMIC_INSTABILITY_SEVERE_FALLS) triggered by complaint 'FALLS': [LLM DRAFT] Recurrent unexplained falls due to sudden severe orthostatic hypotension or profound neurogenic syncope leading to injury or inability to maintain an upright posture..

Other idiopathic peripheral autonomic neuropathy differential diagnosis notes. Compared to History Of Falling: [LLM DRAFT] Episodic loss of balance without prominent systemic autonomic failure symptoms such as anhidrosis or orthostatic hypotension. Compared to Parkinsons Disease Without Dyskinesia With Fluctuations: [LLM DRAFT] Presence of central dopaminergic motor features like resting tremor, rigidity, and bradykinesia accompanying the autonomic symptoms.

Parkinson's disease without dyskinesia, with fluctuations: Parkinson's disease (PD), or simply Parkinson's, is a neurodegenerative disease primarily of the central nervous system, affecting both motor and non-motor systems. The motor symptoms, collectively called parkinsonism, include tremors, slowness in initiating movement (bradykinesia), rigidity, and difficulty maintaining balance. Common presenting complaints: Falls. Associated symptoms: Spasticity, Tremor, Gait Abnormality, Hypokinesia. Risk factors: none listed. Age relevance: . Sex relevance: . Acute or chronic: .

Parkinson's disease without dyskinesia, with fluctuations red flags. Red flag (RF_SEVERE_PARKINSONIAN_CRISIS) triggered by complaint 'FALLS': [LLM DRAFT] Acute, severe worsening of parkinsonian symptoms leading to inability to stand or walk, frequently associated with recurrent falls, trauma, or acute withdrawal/failure of antiparkinsonian medications..

Parkinson's disease without dyskinesia, with fluctuations differential diagnosis notes. Compared to History Of Falling: [LLM DRAFT] Early, frequent falls within the first year of symptom onset suggest atypical parkinsonism rather than Parkinson's disease. Compared to Other Idiopathic Peripheral Autonomic Neuropathy: [LLM DRAFT] Prominent early autonomic failure without central motor signs points toward a peripheral autonomic disorder rather than Parkinson's disease.
